dedupe_keys.name: integrated tsunami risk and agent based evacuation modelling for saga kochi prefecture japan

description: This study builds an integrated tsunami risk framework that combines stochastic tsunami hazard with agent-based evacuation modelling and applies it to Saga, a coastal district of about 2,200 people in Kochi Prefecture, Japan, exposed to magnitude 9 earthquakes. Ario Muhammad, Raffaele De Risi, Flavia De Luca and co-authors from the University of Bristol, Kyoto University, Kansai University and Indonesia's research agency BRIN generated stochastic earthquake sources for magnitudes 8.8 and 9.0 and ran tsunami inundation simulations, then simulated evacuation in MATSim under four scenarios: all on foot, all by car, and two mixes. Combining the two gives risk estimates and tests the benefit of existing evacuation points and towers. Tsunami depths reach up to 15 m with arrival between 5 and 30 minutes; with pedestrian or multimodal evacuation only 10 to 100 people are affected, but up to about 1,000 if the car is the only mode, so walking is recommended along with securing higher ground and vertical evacuation. Coverage: one district, published in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction. Access: open-access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: behavioural parameters are assumed and results apply to this small community. It shows agent-based evacuation and hazard exposure analysis for walking and road networks, and used the MATSim model catalogued here.
